title: 5 Ways the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Game for Nintendo Switch 2 is More Than Just a Remake
summary: The Legend of Zelda™: Ocarina of Time Game for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 System goes beyond a "traditional" remake, revamping the classic game in 5 distinc...
body_markdown:
© Nintendo


The Legend of Zelda™: The Ocarina of Time game is the classic of all classics. You know it. You love it. But wouldn’t it be great to know it and love it all over again? It may be hard to imagine, but from what we’ve seen from the new game for the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system, you might be surprised at how the great minds at Nintendo have found a way to make old feel new again.


**1. Movement and Camera** ****


© Nintendo


Moving. Looking around. Haters will call it basic, but I say how you control your character and camera is an extremely important aspect of your standard action game. Back in the day, however, there was no “standard.” Having a dedicated jump button wasn’t the norm, there was no second analog stick to move the camera, and holding a button down to sprint wasn’t even a thing yet – in Ocarina of Time, we just rolled everywhere!


To make this remake feel fresh, Nintendo is bringing us modern right-stick camera controls, a long-awaited dedicated jump button, and a nostalgia-preserving roll-to-sprint move that is as fun to execute as it is fast and convenient for getting around. Combine that with gyroscope aiming for lining up tricky Hookshot snipes or bow shots and you’ll be moving and maneuvering through Hyrule like a true legendary hero.


**2. Story** ****


**** © Nintendo


The story of Ocarina of Time has always been one of its most lauded aspects. The heroic fantasy of becoming a kingdom-saving legend, the inescapability of time passing, the friends we meet along the way… everything coalesces into one of the all-time most memorable narrative experiences in gaming, at least in this gamer's humble opinion.


However, even if you played Ocarina of Time a million times in the past, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo Switch 2 gives you modern ways to explore that story, adding more depth and perspective to the timeless tale. Characters have expanded and overhauled dialogue, there’s brand new cutscenes to watch, symphonic orchestral music that makes exploring Hyrule all the more epic, and, yes, there’s even voice acting during cutscenes. There are also additional secrets to discover here and there, which only serve to deepen the experience.


**3. Aesthetics**


Okay. I’ve gone long enough without mentioning just how pretty this game looks. Just look at these screenshots.


© Nintendo


© Nintendo


© Nintendo


Yeah. I know, right? Look, I could end this section right here, but I would be remiss if I neglected to point out that the high-fidelity visuals in this game aren’t just there for the spectacle. Rather, the aesthetic choices in this game —spotlights that come down when you target an enemy or open a chest, new dynamic character animations, and cinematic voice-acted cutscenes, to name a few­— all give a theatrical quality to the visual language that makes you feel like you’re in a stage play or a movie rather than “just” a game. I feel like these aesthetics come together to create a new vibe in this release, one you simply couldn’t get from prior releases. ****


**4. New and Reimagined Challenges**


© Nintendo


When it comes to reimagining Ocarina of Time, Nintendo seems to be leaving no stone unturned —or perhaps, no block left un-pushed— even when it comes to the game’s iconic puzzle-solving sections. For one example, the puzzle from the beginning of the game (when Link gets his Kokiri Sword) now requires jumping to complete. Why? Well, that puzzle in the Nintendo 64™ version originally hinged on the player learning the importance of reorienting the camera; however, in this new version, we now have 360-degree control of our camera, rendering that challenge moot. The new jump puzzle echoes the same intention as the original by helping players learn a skill that will be needed throughout their adventure.


For the same reason, it’s safe to expect similar changes to the game’s temples— whether that’s to accommodate for new mechanics like jumping, create useful shortcuts where there weren’t before, add long-awaited quality-of-life improvements (I’m looking at you, Water Temple), or just to add a fresh new take on some familiar puzzles. I think even the most die-hard Legend of Zelda fans will be able to find new things to love in these classic locations.


**5. The Little Things**


**** © Nintendo


Ah. The little things. The fine touches. That’s what really brings it home at the end of the day, isn’t it? There are a ton of little goodies and treats in this new game to be delighted by— like how about a bigger starting wallet? 200 rupees instead of 99 sounds pretty nice. What if the game showed off a satisfying attention to detail— like instead of platforms that float for no reason, there was a large log there instead, or if instead of a ladder that drops from nowhere, it was carefully nestled in a mechanism that you can see releasing the ladder. What a relief that would be. What if you could hum the tune of the ocarina song you needed to play, or even played it on a real instrument, and Link would play that tune in the game? All of these miscellaneous bonuses may seem minor, but collectively they form good old-fashioned icing on top of a good old -


fashioned cake. What a treat.


**What’s Old Is Young Again** **** © Nintendo


By now, I think it’s clear: this ain’t your Unc’s Ocarina of Time. This Ocarina of Time is expertly crafted to shine with today’s gamers in mind, while still delivering on what made the original so special in the first place. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time may be a game that most gamers know inside and out. But with all of the fresh additions the Nintendo Switch™ 2 version adds, I truly believe you’ll get to know and love one of the greatest games of all time all over again, and there’s something really special about that.
